cost: THE PIN SITS ON ITS EDGE. LeBron James '04 def 70 +-2 is added at a reading of 68, error exactly -2. The ceiling is not clause 1: recal_93's MIDDLE clause grades him 0.4286 big on rimprot 60 / 3pt 26 by itself, and d_bigness combines the clauses by max(), so no change to clause 1 can take him past DEF 68. A later round that wants 70 exactly must reopen recal_93's ramp, and this round did not.

No anchor was re-derived and no band anchor was touched: OFF_TOP and DEF_TOP are byte-identical, so nothing above the knee moved. is_big is untouched, so OFF, every attribute, the big flag, the big hub, the stretch-big floor and the OVR cap branch are all unchanged — OFF moves on ZERO of 10,000 cards.

EQUALITY NOW READS ZERO. The old test included `>=`, so a card with rimprot EXACTLY equal to perdef took the whole big verdict; on a ramp from a gap of 0 it takes none of it. That is the whole point of the round (a claim of zero separation is a claim of zero), but it is the one place where the change is not a small one for a small input: Reggie Williams '89 (54/54) +6 and J.J. Anderson '83 (53/53) +6 are the two largest movers on the board and both are equality cards.

Tayshaun Prince is the class that pays for it: '04 78 -> 76, '05 72 -> 70, '10 65 -> 63, '11 63 -> 60, '06 64 -> 63, and '12 58 -> 56 — a wing whose rim protection runs a point or two over his perimeter defence is no longer graded entirely on the big vector. '16 goes the other way (+4) because there the big vector was the lower one. None of the six is pinned.
notes: THE DEFECT. LeBron James '04 reads rimprot 60 against perdef 59. Sixty is past recal_136's saturation at 55, so that ramp returns 1.00 and the SHAPE test alone decided him — and it answered one point of separation with a hard 1.0. He was graded on the whole big vector, 57.92 x 1.1305 = 65, while his own perimeter vector reads 62.01 x 1.1305 = 70. His neighbouring seasons sit on the other side of the same one-point line: '05 (rimprot 61 < perdef 65) is 100% perimeter at 77, '06 perimeter at 82, '07 92% perimeter at 89.

THE FIX, AND IT INTRODUCES NO NEW CONSTANT. `rimprot >= perdef` becomes min(1, max(0, (rimprot - perdef) / (C1_RP_HI - C1_RP_LO))) — a ramp on the signed gap over recal_136's OWN ramp width, 10. At a gap of 10 or more the clause returns exactly what it always did. The clause's other two tests are untouched: `3pt < 45` is still hard and recal_136's rim-protection ramp still multiplies. LeBron '04's branch weight goes 1.0000 -> 0.4286 (the floor set by recal_93's middle clause) and DEF 65 -> 68.

WHY THIS CLAUSE. recal_93 ramped the middle clause, recal_99 the deterrence clause, recal_136 clause 1's rim-protection bar — each round wrote in its own comment that this shape test was left hard. It was the last hard 1.0 in the function.

THE WIDER WIDTH, MEASURED AND REJECTED. The clause's own DEF_RP band (35) gives the subject the same 68 (his ceiling is elsewhere) but takes recal_136's own subject Ken Norman '94 from 53 to 49, outside his 55 +-3; a width of 20 takes him to 51, also outside. Ten is both the width the clause already carries and the widest the anchors permit.

MEASURED ON THE WHOLE POOL: 45 of 10,000 cards move on DEF, 22 up and 23 down, max +6 / -3; OFF and every attribute move on ZERO; OVR follows on 28, max 3. The top 12 by DEF is identical. All 154 standing anchors pass (mean |error| 0.79). The movers are one archetype and it is the archetype recal_72 named when it wrote this clause — 'SF-only stoppers (Reggie Williams-class)': Reggie Williams '89 himself, Tayshaun Prince, Lionel Simmons, Derrick McKey, Boris Diaw, Josh Howard, Deni Avdija '23, Josh Giddey '22.
The tactics harness passes on all nine dials with no tax re-sweep.
